chats.answer:
A small portable power station with a 245–300 Wh battery can typically keep a Wi-Fi router and modem running for about 10–15 hours during a power outage. The exact runtime depends on how much electricity your equipment consumes and the power station's own energy losses.

Based on the search results, my top pick is the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2, especially if you want your Wi-Fi to stay connected automatically when the electricity goes out.

Best small power stations for Wi-Fi backup

1. BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 — Best overall

288 Wh battery · 10 ms or less UPS switchover

~12 hours

At a 20 W router-and-modem load. Includes 12 V DC outputs that can help reduce power losses.

2. EcoFlow RIVER 3 — Compact alternative

245 Wh battery · UPS switchover varies by version

~10 hours

At 20 W. Lightweight and compact, but check the version's switchover specification.

3. Tenergy T320 — Another 300 Wh option

300 Wh battery · UPS switchover not specified

~12.5 hours

At 20 W. Suitable for battery backup, though seamless switchover is not established.

These are published estimates from Dealectric's November 2026 comparison. They are not independently verified runtime tests. 
Dealectric
+1

How long will your Wi-Fi actually last?

A typical router and modem together consume approximately 10–20 watts. Here is an illustrative estimate for a 288 Wh battery, assuming 85% usable energy and excluding additional standby consumption.

What matters most when choosing?

UPS functionality: A fast switchover helps prevent your router from restarting during an outage.

DC power outputs: Powering compatible routers directly from DC can avoid the inverter's energy losses.

Internet provider availability: Your router can remain powered while your ISP's neighborhood equipment loses electricity, leaving you without internet access.

My recommendation: Choose the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 for a compact, roughly half-day Wi-Fi backup solution. If your only goal is to keep a router and modem online, a dedicated mini UPS may be a more economical option.

The search also found that a larger 500–700 Wh station can provide substantially longer backup, potentially more than a day depending on the load.

chats.answer:
For keeping a Wi-Fi router and cable modem running during a power outage, you don't need a large power station. A compact 150–300Wh portable power station is usually enough to keep your internet running for 6–15 hours, depending on your equipment.

How long will a power station run your Wi-Fi?

A typical home setup consumes:

Wi-Fi router: 8–15 watts

Cable modem: 5–12 watts

Combined: approximately 15–25 watts
